default.value:
node = nuke.thisNode() 
node['licenseCheckTrigger'].execute() 
licenseCheckResult = bool(node['licenseCheckResult'].getValue()) 
if licenseCheckResult: 
  previewKnob = node['preview'] 
  previewKnob.setValue(0) 
  keysKnob = node['keyFrame'] 
  detectionFrameType = int(node['detectionFrameType'].getValue()) 
  thisFrame = nuke.frame() 
  if detectionFrameType == 0: 
    keysKnob.setKeyAt(thisFrame) 
    frameRange = nuke.FrameRanges([thisFrame]) 
    nuke.execute(node, frameRange) 
  else: 
    spacing = int(node['detectionFrameSpacing'].getValue()) 
    keys = list(set(list(range(thisFrame, node.firstFrame() - 1, -spacing)) + list(range(thisFrame, node.lastFrame() + 1, spacing)))) 
    keys.sort() 
    frameRange = nuke.FrameRanges(keys) 
    for i in keys: 
      keysKnob.setKeyAt(i) 
    nuke.execute(node, frameRange)

Set the base exponent of the radial distortion polynomial.

The first term controls the numerator exponents and the second controls the denominator exponents.

Note: a base exponent of 2 for the denominator corresponds to the classic NukeX model.

Set the distortion model direction.

A 'Forward' model is estimated directly but needs to be inverted for image rendering. Conversely, a 'Backward' model is estimated via its inverse but can be used directly for image rendering. Model inversion is not an exact process and might cause loss of information due to approximations.

Note: the classic NukeX model is a 'Forward' model.

Distortion model equation display.

Legend: (xd, yd) are the distorted cartesian coordinates, (rd, phid) are the distorted polar coordinates, (xu, yu) are the undistorted cartesian coordinates, (ru, phiu) are the undistorted polar coordinates, and the k-values are the distortion coefficients. The coordinate systems are relative to the distortion centre.

In this case, you can choose to scale to the specified format.

Control the error threshold for outliers rejection.

Decrease for a closer fit, but with the risk of overfitting. Too many outliers can signal an issue with the distortion model.

Control the distance between detected feature points.

This value should reflect the scale of an square element of the grid.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Select the output mode to undistort or redistort footage.

Choose 'STMap' to render both undistortion and redistortion STMaps in the 'motion' channels. Use the 'forward' channels for undistorting and the 'backward' channels for redistorting. The other input channels are copied to the output directly. In this mode, the overlay grids can be displayed on top of the source image. Choose the 'Undistort' option to undistort the input directly. Select what to display in the overlay.

Choose 'Features' to view detected feature points only. Only features are editable in this mode. Deleting a feature will not delete the link it belongs to. Choose 'Links' to only display the links between feature points. Only links are editable in this mode. Deleting a link will not delete the features it connects. Choose 'All' to display both feature points and links. When this option is selected, both types can be edited at the same time.

Estimate the distortion model parameters using the detected grids or manually drawn lines.

At least as many feature links as parameters in the distortion model are needed to enable 'Solve'. In case you don't have enough links, try to draw more lines, add more keyframes for detection, or tune the detection parameters.

The solver tries to warp the distorted links to straight lines. If the result is not satifying, try to press 'Solve' again to refine.

Root mean square (RMS) solve error in pixels.

This can be used to measure the quality of the solve. It is computed as the average deviation to an ideal straight line for each link. Move the mouse over a link to display its individual residual error.

Choose whether lens projection should be considered as part of the distortion.

Enable to defish a fisheye image when undistorting, and refish when redistorting. Disable to render an ideal fisheye without distortion when undistorting, and apply distortion to a fisheye image when redistorting. This has no effect for rectilinear lenses.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: LensDistortion: Estimates, removes and applies lens distortion. Lens: Set up the lens characteristics and the distortion model parameters. Keyframes: Set keyframes on a grid shot for multi-grid analysis. Analysis: Run grid detector and distortion solver. Set grid detection options on the dedicated tab. Output: Set the image rendering options to undistort or redistort the footage. STMaps in the 'motion' channels can be used separately to the same effect.
